## What This Is

Three new cheat sheets added to Getting Started, plus targeted refinements to Session 0 and Session 1 based on real first-session learnings. These additions address the most common friction points encountered during initial setup — cloud sync traps, commit timing, permission approvals, and mobile sync configuration. The Getting Started folder now includes reference material that answers questions people ask before they know they need to ask them.

## What It Adds / Changes

- New: `Cheat Sheet - Tool Roles.md` — answers "why do I need so many programs?" with one paragraph per tool, Mac and Windows noted, and a summary table including the Claude Code Notifier extension
- New: `Cheat Sheet - Claude Code Quick Reference.md` — session start, permission approvals ("yes" vs "yes allow for this project"), session closeout, commit strategy, cost awareness, and Claude Code Notifier note
- New: `Cheat Sheet - Common Setup Issues.md` — six friction points from real sessions converted into preventive guidance: cloud sync folder trap, Obsidian Sync vault password distinction, Windows git safe.directory fix, VS Code folder selection, ChatGPT export async timing, commit deferral during setup
- Session 0: added cloud sync pre-flight check to the checklist and ChatGPT async export timing note (3–12 hours, start early)
- Session 1: added permission approval explanation, commit strategy deferral note, and optional Mobile Setup section covering Obsidian Sync and vault password
- Getting Started Index: new Cheat Sheets section with links to all three files

## How to Implement

1. Pull the latest changes: run the Ecosystem Update Check skill or `git pull origin master` in your ecosystem folder.
2. The three cheat sheets will appear in your `Getting Started/` folder automatically.
3. Open `Getting Started/Index.md` to see them listed in the new Cheat Sheets section.
4. Read `Cheat Sheet - Common Setup Issues.md` before your next setup session to pre-empt the most common friction points.
5. No existing governance files are affected. No token replacements needed.

## Prerequisites

None. Applies to all builds at any stage.

## Optional?

No — these are foundational Getting Started improvements recommended for all builds.
